Week 2: Dome, MPE Calibration, and the Closed Loop

Visual reference boards and Godot 4 integration notes for all five Week 2 milestones—unifying terrarium husbandry, DriftingSensor guardbands, bench calibration, optical silk, and farm-to-dome swapping.

One DriftingSensor model for every instrument

Moving both the terrarium hygrometer and the rover steering encoder onto a single reusable DriftingSensor component is the smartest architectural call you can make in Week 2. Every future instrument—temperature probes, dish azimuth encoders, alien gauges—automatically inherits the exact same sensor_drift_config.json math, guardbands, and bench UI.

Instrument Instance Unit & Nominal Sample MPE When Out of Tolerance (> MPE)
Terrarium Hygrometer 65.0 %RH ±5.0 %RH Molt progress pauses; heat lamp tint shifts harsh amber; enclosure LED blinks red.
Rover Steering Encoder 0.0 deg ±4.0 deg Tractor visibly pulls off-line while tilling; phone HUD flashes an out-of-spec warning.

The bench calibration station UI

When the player clicks the calibration bench (or brings an instrument to it), open a crisp centered desktop overlay modeled on real bench metrology gear: As-Found on the left, As-Left on the right, and a tactile zeroing action that logs the pass/fail against MPE.

1. Snapshot As-Found

The moment you open the bench for a sensor, freeze its current drifted reading into as_found_value and stamp whether it arrived In Tolerance or OOT (which later feeds MegaCorp audit logs).

2. Zero to As-Left

Let the player drag a rotary knob or hold a "Zero & Trim" button until the needle settles inside the green MPE band, recording as_left_value (with a tiny realistic residual noise like ±0.2 so it feels authentic).

3. Visual LED sync

Closing the bench immediately flips the tiny 3D emissive LED on the terrarium pod (or the phone steering indicator) back to crisp emerald green so the world reflects your calibration.

Closing the loop: molt, optical silk, and relay lag

Milestone 4 is the magic moment where your two pillars become one game. Keeping the terrarium hygrometer in-band fills a molt progress meter; when the tarantula molts, it drops one Optical Silk Spool that you slot directly into the farm's satellite relay to slash rover input lag.

Terrarium molt state machine (greybox-ready)

Start with three simple visual states on your placeholder tarantula: Active (normal color), Pre-Molt (curled or dimmed while timer > 80%), and Molted (spawns a small translucent pale cube beside it plus a glowing cyan cylinder for the collectible silk spool).

Relay upgrade payoff on the farm

When you walk up to or click the outdoor SatelliteRelay with a spool in inventory, snap the cyan spool mesh onto its side bay, turn the relay's beacon brighter cyan, and apply lag_reduction_pct (for example, cutting occluded lag from 0.45s down to 0.18s).

Switching cleanly between the farm and the dome

A simple scene swap between main_farm.tscn and dome_interior.tscn is all you need in Week 2—as long as your live simulation state lives in an autoload singleton so nothing resets when you cross the airlock.

Keep state in GameState autoload

Store hygrometer_state, steering_sensor_state, molt_progress, optical_silk_count, and relay_upgraded in a persistent GameState.gd autoload—never inside the scene nodes themselves—so sensors keep ticking even while you are in the other scene.

Two-way swap trigger

Place a clickable glowing airlock hatch in both scenes (and bind a quick desktop shortcut like Tab or a phone button) calling get_tree().change_scene_to_file() with a brief 0.2s fade so jumping back and forth feels snappy during playtesting.

Week 2 handoff prompt for Claude

Paste this straight into your existing Claude session to implement all five Week 2 items cleanly on top of your Week 1 Godot 4 project.

We're ready to build Week 2 of our desktop-only Godot 4 (GDScript, Forward+) vertical slice for "Out of Spec." Let's implement these 5 pieces cleanly on top of Week 1:

1. Persistent `GameState.gd` autoload:
   - Holds live state across scene swaps: `DriftingSensor` data for both `terrarium_hygrometer` and `rover_steering`, `molt_progress` (0.0 to 1.0), `optical_silk_spools` count, `relay_slotted` bool, and `last_cal_records` (As-Found, As-Left, pass/fail vs. MPE).
   - Advances sensor drift and molt progress inside `_process(delta)` so timers keep ticking regardless of whether the player is on the farm or in the dome.

2. Reusable `DriftingSensor.gd` (Resource or RefCounted class) driven by `data/sensor_drift_config.json`:
   - Evaluates status band against `mpe`: `IN_BAND` (|err| <= 0.7 * mpe), `GUARDBAND` (0.7 * mpe < |err| <= mpe), `OUT_OF_TOLERANCE` (|err| > mpe).
   - Migrate Week 1's `rover_controller.gd` steering drift onto this exact same `DriftingSensor` instance.

3. `scenes/dome_interior.tscn`:
   - Greybox cozy dome room with: (a) one clear glass terrarium box, warm amber OmniLight3D heat lamp, placeholder cobalt tarantula mesh, and a tiny emissive status LED synced to the hygrometer band; (b) a clickable bench calibration station; (c) a clickable airlock door back to `main_farm.tscn`.

4. Bench Calibration Station UI (`ui/cal_bench_ui.tscn`):
   - Lets the player select an instrument (Terrarium Hygrometer or Rover Steering).
   - Displays As-Found reading, MPE tolerance limit, live color-coded status band (Green/Amber/Red), and a "Zero / Calibrate" control that records As-Left (within MPE) and resets drift.

5. Molt, Optical Silk & Relay Upgrade + Scene Swap:
   - While `terrarium_hygrometer` is IN_BAND or GUARDBAND (<= MPE), `molt_progress` fills (use a fast test duration like 20 seconds so we can playtest immediately).
   - At 100%, spawn a clickable glowing cyan `OpticalSilkSpool` next to the tarantula; clicking adds +1 spool to `GameState`.
   - On `main_farm.tscn`, clicking the `SatelliteRelay` while holding a spool slots it in (`relay_slotted = true`), brightens the relay beacon, and cuts rover input lag by `lag_reduction_pct` from `tarantula_species.json`.
   - Add a clickable airlock door in both scenes (plus a Tab hotkey) to swap smoothly between `main_farm.tscn` and `dome_interior.tscn`.

“Once your recalibrated hygrometer drops a silk spool that visibly cuts rover lag outside, the entire game’s thesis is proven.”

Keep the Week 2 molt timer short (15–20 seconds) during testing so you can feel the full dome → bench → molt → farm relay loop in under two minutes.
